title: Install Emailer Ripe
subtitle: Version 1.3.0 | Beginner guide | Ubuntu Apache or Debian Nginx VPS

blocks.text: Install a usable Emailer Ripe website with one guided server setup. You need your administrator email, a new password, and the address you want people to use. Email delivery can wait.

Ubuntu Apache can coexist with Nginx on a separate port (tested: 8081). Setup manages only Apache and the Emailer instance. Every existing listener on ports 80 and 443 must belong to apache2.service; a different service on either port or an overlapping Emailer hostname stops setup with existing services preserved. Ripe additionally supports literal IPv4/IPv6 Apache virtual hosts on explicit ports 80 and 443. Fresh setup joins the existing address groups automatically. Updates and Light upgrades retain the existing Emailer site’s address bindings. Its dedicated file must group addresses into at most one VirtualHost block per port; custom routing or separate blocks on the same port require operator preparation. Wildcard-port virtual hosts (IP:*) and scoped addresses are unsupported; setup stops before changing websites.
Who can use this guide?

Use a virtual server with Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS and Apache, or Debian 13 and Nginx. It must be amd64/x86-64, use systemd, and let you run sudo. Setup chooses Apache on a clean Ubuntu host and Nginx on a clean Debian 13 host. The tested server has 2 CPU cores, 3 GB memory and a 24 GB disk. Ubuntu 22.04 needs at least 5 GiB free; other supported profiles need 2 GiB. Leave additional space for uploads and backups.

An existing Apache website using PHP 8.1 can stay on Ubuntu 22.04, including its existing database and unrelated services. Give Emailer a spare hostname. Setup adds its own PHP runtime and application services without changing the existing website’s PHP selection. Ubuntu 22.04 also gets a separate supported database; it does not upgrade an older shared database. Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 reuse a compatible local MariaDB server. An incompatible existing database on those two profiles stops setup before packages change.

blocks.text: Only these OS/web-server combinations are supported. Ubuntu using Nginx as its public web server on ports 80/443, Debian 13 with Apache, ARM, custom website ports/subfolders and ordinary file-upload hosting are outside this installer’s tested scope. On a VPS that also hosts other websites, Emailer needs its own dedicated hostname; existing websites retain their configuration and operation.

Ordinary file-upload/shared hosting cannot run this installer: Emailer needs a persistent background worker, scheduled services and private key storage outside the website. Uploading PHP files alone cannot provide these requirements. Use the supported VPS path.

On Ubuntu, setup adds the maintained Ondřej Surý PHP package source and verifies its signing identity automatically. Ubuntu 22.04’s separate database receives security patches through reviewed Emailer maintenance releases, rather than the server’s ordinary package updates. Keep Emailer maintenance releases current; you do not need to assemble or configure the database yourself.
1. Get your server and website address ready

Sign in to your hosting provider's server console or use its SSH instructions. This is the terminal where you paste the setup action below. You need the provider's server sign-in; it is separate from the new Emailer account.

Choose a spare address such as news.your-domain.com. In your domain provider's DNS controls, point its A record to this server's public IPv4 address. Add an AAAA record only if this server actually accepts public IPv6. Allow incoming TCP ports 80 and 443 in the hosting firewall. Do not take over an existing website address. Setup cannot edit your domain or hosting-provider account without access to that account.
2. Download the official setup package

While signed in to GitHub with access to the private Emailer Ripe release, download emailer-ripe-1.3.0-setup.run. Upload that one file to the server using your provider's file-transfer facility. An authorized privately supplied copy of the same signed setup file also works. Keep the file private. Do not paste a GitHub token or repository password into a download command.
You do not need a source checkout, Composer, a public-key file or separate verification sidecars. Those components are inside the setup package.

Initial trust comes from obtaining the setup action itself from the official HTTPS release or an authorized private channel. Its embedded, established edition signing identity then verifies the package inventory, runtime and release identity before installer code runs. A key supplied beside an arbitrary download would not establish that initial trust.

Ubuntu 22.04 also retrieves an authenticated MariaDB runtime of about 360 MB. Allow time for this download; progress is saved and an interrupted download resumes when you start the same setup file again. No container software or Composer command is needed.
3. Start setup
From the folder containing the downloaded file, paste this single setup action:
sudo sh emailer-ripe-1.3.0-setup.run

If setup finds an existing Light installation, choose Install a separate fresh Ripe application for this fresh-install guide. Choose its upgrade option only when you intend to convert Light, following the separate upgrade guide. The fresh Ripe site needs a different dedicated hostname.

sudo may ask for your server account password once. Setup needs host permission to install services; the application itself runs under a dedicated account. Keep the terminal open. Password entry is hidden, so no letters or dots may appear.

items: Enter Application hostname if asked: just your dedicated address, without https://, a port or a path. Setup does not assume the machine's name is a public website.
Enter Owner email. This becomes your sign-in name.
Enter a strong Owner password and enter it again. Use 15-256 characters.

On Ubuntu 22.04 fresh setup creates its own database without asking for database details. On Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 13, enter a database administrator sign-in only if the existing local MariaDB server needs it; passwords are hidden.

blocks.text: You will see named progress steps for dependencies, package verification, private folders, database and account, services, backup/recovery, HTTPS and health. Organisation name defaults to Emailer; language to English and scheduling timezone to UTC. SMTP details are not required.

blocks.caption: Actual Ripe setup completion. Use the login address printed by your own installation.

blocks.text: 4. Sign in

Wait for Installation successful. Open the printed HTTPS login address in your browser and sign in with the email and password you entered. Setup has already installed the worker, scheduler, maintenance jobs and command launcher and verified the initial backup. Do not proceed past a browser certificate warning; use the HTTPS troubleshooting entry below.

blocks.caption: Actual Ripe dashboard after sign-in with email delivery deferred.

blocks.text: 5. Configure email now or later
You can prepare templates and draft campaigns immediately. Email delivery is not configured means actual sending is blocked. No campaign is approved or sent during installation.

When ready, open Settings & tools > Mail settings. Use your provider's outgoing-mail server, port, encryption, username, SMTP password/key and permitted sender address. The sender name is optional. Saving encrypts the settings; it sends nothing. Choose Test connection without sending to check secure connection and sign-in. To send one message, enter your own address in Test destination and explicitly choose Send test email.

blocks.caption: Actual Mail settings screen. A connection test sends no message; sending a test email is a separate explicit action.

blocks.text: Ripe starts at High security. Before sending, open Settings & tools > MFA, confirm your current credentials when asked, and start enrollment. Add the displayed setup key to an authenticator app, save the recovery codes privately, enter its current code and confirm. Treat that screen as secret; do not share a screenshot. Existing accounts keep their login identifiers.

blocks.caption: Actual MFA status after enrollment. The setup key and recovery codes are not shown in this screenshot.

blocks.text: 6. Keep your recovery information

The completion summary gives your verified backup folder, local backup destination, encrypted recovery-key package and protected recovery-password file. These paths are created automatically. Keep a separate, securely stored copy of the recovery package and its password, using different protected locations. A backup on the same server cannot protect you from losing the server.

For a fresh Ripe installation, backups are under /var/lib/emailer/private/backups, the local destination is /var/backups/emailer, the recovery package is /var/lib/emailer/keys/recovery-key.enxkey, and the password is /var/lib/emailer-installer/recovery-password. Host permission is needed to read the password. Never paste it into a support ticket. After updates or edition changes, use the locations printed by that operation.
If setup stops

head: What you see
Smallest next action
rows: Correct the domain records and provider firewall for this server, then run the same setup action again. Saved progress is retained. HTTPS is complete only after validation succeeds.
Keep that service running. Existing supported Apache/Nginx sites can coexist; a different service owning the web ports needs a separate supported VPS. Setup does not stop unrelated services.

Ubuntu 22.04 provisions its own isolated database. On Ubuntu 24.04 or Debian 13, an incompatible existing server is preserved; use the supported separate VPS profile rather than upgrading a shared database during setup.
Signed OS package catalogue cannot be used
Check the server clock, internet connection and configured OS repositories. Setup does not bypass signature checks. Keep the same setup file and retry.
Package authenticity or integrity verification failed
Delete only the failed download, obtain a fresh official setup file, and retry. Keep any existing application and recovery files.
Run the same action again. It resumes the recorded setup; it does not create another administrator or reset an existing database.

blocks.text: Run setup again for installation management. Check the installation is safe to repeat; an installed update preserves settings and delivery state. For other errors, read the operator and troubleshooting reference. Keep installer state and database files when retrying. Next: Ripe user manual.
